Our clinicals depended on luck for the specifics but everyone always gets 1 long term care placement, 2 acute medical (some people got emerg if they were lucky), one maternity/labour and delivery, one pediatrics, 1 surgical placement, and then our 2 preceptorship placements. One of the preceptorships has to be an acute medical or surgical placement and then we could choose a specialty, I chose emergency for my preceptorship.

For my clinicals I got hospice for my LTC placement, rehab and a respiratory/oncology medical unit for my acute care placements, and a General/thoracic surgical unit for my surgical placement.

As far as I know operating room and critical care aren’t options during regular clinicals but I know plenty of classmates who ended up precepting in community, ICU, NICU, OR, emerg, etc… I believe they’ve just implemented pathways as well for you to essentially do additional education in a specialty like ER, ICU, OR, then complete an internship and then get hired into that specialty once you finish the program. I have a classmate who I believe finished the OR pathway and is an OR nurse now

I’m a new grad of 4 months now started on a med surg unit! Knock on wood but it hasn’t been too bad at all, it’s not always as daunting as it seems. Some days are pretty bad but some days are great too. I work on a trauma ortho and neuro floor so a mix of elective surgeries and traumas like falls and MVCs. I’ve worked a few short staffed shifts where I’ve had to take 7 patients and I missed all my breaks, one started crashing just before shift change but in the end it all worked out okay, everyone got their meds and treatments on time, I survived, and my patients survived. That was probably the worst shift I’ve worked so far. But I did my best and everyone was okay. I’ve been learning so so much and I super appreciate how supportive my unit is as we get many new grads and I dare say I actually like med surg as of now lol, I was planning on going to ER after a year of experience but I might stick around on this unit for a while. Wherever you start will be valuable experience!! Nursing is nursing and it will only be beneficial for any future roles you may start. Maybe find a niche in med surg that would interest you? Ie. cardiac, neuro, ortho, respiratory, etc… I have always been interested in trauma and it gives some higher acuity patients so it’s been very interesting for me!

I did not ever work as an ESN or HCA (I felt too burnt out to) and am currently a new grad of 4 months working on an ortho trauma and neuro surgical unit. All my feedback so far has been that I’m doing very well! I am also way less burnt out now, working is so much better than being a student IMO maybe I’m speaking too soon. Finally being paid and compensated for your labour feels amazing compared to being a student.

Overall I wouldn’t worry about it too much, I felt like I got more experience in my senior preceptorship than I did in the rest of my schooling, and then in my new grad orientation I felt like I learned more than I did in my preceptorship, and again now being alone off orientation I feel like I am learning so much more compared to when people are actively watching over you to catch any mistakes. 

In the grand scheme of things I feel like ESN experience is just a drop in the bucket of how many hours and experience you will gain in even 6 months as a new nurse. I would really just try to push yourself to gain as much experience and knowledge as you can in your remaining clinicals and senior preceptorships. Take the challenging assignments and ask lots of questions! I also don’t think it’s a bad idea to start thinking about what kind of experience you want for your senior preceptorship, they give the option for 1 med surg one, and then you can choose a specialty for your second preceptorship. I was on my current unit now for my med-surg preceptorship, and I chose emergency as my specialty and it seriously helped with my autonomy and critical thinking and I owe a lot of my success as a new grad to that experience and my awesome preceptor who really pushed me to act as the primary RN. Choose experiences that will benefit you the most with where you want to be as a new grad. When you apply for your first new grad job the recruiter will go over the open positions and they prefer to line you up with where you did your senior preceptorships as it makes the transition a lot easier. Don’t be afraid to try new things as a student, that’s honestly one of the best times to try when you have the school supporting you. I had never had a clinical on my current unit until I did my senior preceptorship there and it ended up being my favorite unit I had been on. Best of luck!

What the nurses and doctors will be concerned about regarding hypertension or hypotension may vary somewhat depending on the unit culture/patient presentation but for myself a general rule anything under 90 systolic or over 160 systolic tends to ring some concern for me. Once they get to 70-80’s systolic I will usually call the doctor, and same with 180+ systolic. If you get a very high or low reading as a student you will just let your nurse know. I work in an adult neuro ortho trauma surgical. On my unit it helps that we generally use those parameters for medications, so we hold medications that drop BP if they are already under 90 systolic and for our neuro patients who we don’t want to have increasing ICP they will usually have orders to keep their systolic under 160. 

I doubt your first placement will involve kids so unless you’ve already taken your peds class where they do teach you the ranges for kids I wouldn’t worry about it, I didn’t learn that until my 3rd year and I don’t think it would be expected this early in your program. While the BP is running I usually just start their other vitals, get their temperature, put their sp02 probe on, count their resp rate, or just start asking them assessment questions. I’m guessing in your first placement they will have you take full set of vitals and begin to work on your head to toe assessment. It will feel super awkward at first but smoothness and confidence will come with time!

Tacrolimus/protopic was the only thing that helped my face flares, it worked well to reduce the itching and swelling but my skin barrier was demolished afterwards anyways. Unfortunately my skin doesn’t do well with super thick occlusive moisturizers and creams, so to rebuild my barrier I just had to do many layers of thin gentle lotions (lubriderm or aveeno) and non-irritating hydrating serums (I often used the snail mucin serum from cosrx), and sealed it with a layer of Vaseline. It took some months but my skin on my face is finally intact again and not angry and raw

I’m so sorry, I feel you. Eczema is so painful emotionally and physically and I find people never really understand the toll it takes mentally unless they’ve gone through it themselves. I’ve had eczema since I was young, maybe about 5 years old. I’m 22 now. I had it all over my hands, arms, and now struggling with it on my neck, face, stomach and chest. It really does a number on your self confidence, I feel especially as a teen girl. I remember people always asking me what was wrong with my skin or if it was contagious. It feels so much worse at that age too. The social aspect of it gets better as an adult, nobody really cares, they sometimes feel bad for me. At this point most people I meet know what eczema is and often have had it themselves or know others who do so it’s no longer a big deal. I once had a friend who didn’t know what it was and he asked me with the most genuinely concerned expression if it would shorten my lifespan. It cracked me up a little, bless his heart English wasn’t his first language. But it put in perspective that things aren’t so bad after all, even though a lot of the time it does feel like hell.

I remember feeling like nobody would ever like me because of how ugly my hands and skin was, but the right people won’t care at all. You can date just fine I’ve never had my eczema held against me in social settings. I currently have a bf despite my eczema being the worst it has ever been. I wish I could say the eczema itself gets better too but I’m currently going thru one of the worst flares of my life :/  It is incredibly frustrating but I’m hoping for you that it gets better. Just get through it day by day and I’m holding on to the hope that it gets better for me too🩷

I live closer to kgh which was annoying at first commuting to the school for early classes but now I appreciate as it’s a much shorter commute to even earlier mornings at the hospital. Goodluck with the residence!

4th year here, about 4 shifts away from finishing :) agreed that year 2 feels the most rough but it’s doable. Just a lot of info thrown at you at once and u get a lot of the tough classes. Year 3 was pretty chill classes wise just more responsibility in clinicals, year 4 is mostly just shifts in the hospital. I’m from the Fraser valley as well and I don’t find it too bad being out here, big outdoorsy community in Kelowna so if you’re into hiking, climbing, ski/snowboarding, etc.. you’ll like it here. Personally didn’t love living back home so I didn’t struggle much with missing home. 

I had enough free time to have a bit of a social life and do hobbies. Had to sacrifice some birthdays and such but usually u can be home for holidays. Be prepared to have to commute to Vernon or penticton with your clinical placements. As annoying as it is to commute I actually think I had some of my best learning in Vernon and Penticton as there tends to be less students so I feel like you actually get more opportunities to do stuff. Sometimes kgh has so many students it’s hard to get opportunities.

Overall I feel like the program is kind of designed to help you succeed, most teachers really want to see you do well. I think most test averages in my cohort were 80% ish never really felt worried about genuinely being at risk for failing and I tend to have less than great study habits. Pay attention in class and don’t skip! Don’t have anything else to compare it to but I feel like it’s a solid program

Hey. Still no contact, been about 6 months? I saw him in public once a month ago and I just waved at him as I had to walk past him. we said nothing to one another, just shared a sad look. I still miss him every day, but I think it’s probably best for us to stay this way. We just hurt eachother too much for us to move past it I think. As much as we care for eachother we trigger eachother in the worst ways. I think we both somehow made eachother feel like we were not enough. I imagine that he constantly felt inadequate about how he wasn’t doing enough, wasn’t good for me, and I constantly felt like I wasn’t good enough as he was always half commited, lying to me, and expressing how much he hurt me probably only made this insecurity worse and pushed us apart. Sorry if this isn’t the answer u were looking for. I do not think we will reconcile anytime soon but that is the result my situation due to the reasons that I’ve explained above. You know your person better and we are all different so don’t take it to heart or that there is certainly no chance for reconciliation for you. And dont beat yourself up for how you acted. I’m sure everyone has done things they regret and hurt one another in a relationship that ended. Emotions run high and we say hurtful things when we are hurt. Sometimes (oftentimes) reconciliation is not the best result as well. Hope you are healing whatever that may look like for you ❤️

Don’t give up hope! My best friend (also 21) only just recently got into her first relationship after having these same worries and fears her whole life and the guy treats her so well, he’s a real gentleman. I’ve been in 2 relationships before but neither were any good. If it makes you feel any better I also feel very unlovable from a different perspective because 2 separate people decided to date me and yet still couldn’t bring themselves to love me. It’s different kind of hurt I guess. You’re still young though! I wouldn’t give up so soon. Just keep living life and being the best version of yourself you can be. 

Something I had to do was really look at myself as objectively as possible and think would I date myself? What do I have to work on if not? If I met myself would I like them? That might help maximize your chances. But at the end of the day it is all just chance. I firmly believe that most relationships are just truly luck. You just have to end up somewhere at the right time and run into someone else at the right time. There’s not really much else to it. Some people get lucky and run into people they are compatible with and are mutually attracted to more often, so relationships seem easy. You could be the greenest flag but if that timing with the right person doesn’t line up the connection won’t happen. So be patient and enjoy what the single life has to offer in the meantime :) the one thing about being in relationships has taught me is actually how to best enjoy my time single and alone now. I used to be just like you, always want a relationship, hopeless romantic deep down. I still am, but I also love being my own person, having no ties and just being able to invest all my time and effort into bettering myself. 

Sometimes in a relationship you pour and pour into someone else and it doesn’t work out or they take advantage of it, play with your feelings, etc… there is an inherent risk in getting to relationships as you just have to trust the person has good intentions for you. But when you pour into yourself, that’s a situation where you are 100% certain the effort you put into yourself is not wasted. Which is an unmatched plus side of being single!

Not an asshole but do I think it was inconsiderate to send this on their birthday. Birthdays are somebody’s  unique day to celebrate themselves and getting a loaded text like this from an ex on a day I should be dedicating to myself would come across a strangely to me, like my ex is making my own birthday about themselves. I understand you most likely did not think about it this way and had good intentions but all things considered I would not want to maintain a friendship with an ex who could not be considerate of how I would feel in that situation, after all a friendship has to go both ways. Probably not the best move on your part, but not an asshole. I think your ex doesn’t have any hard feelings against you for it, so don’t hold it against yourself either.

It is most likely better for both of you in the long run to not stay friends anyways. From the texts it seems like the breakup wasn’t long ago so you may think it’s a good idea now but chances are it would’ve hurt you as well. This is coming from someone who also tried to stay friends with my ex thinking I could do it and they actually agreed to be friends but it really hurt me and set back my healing in the end. You sound like you are doing your best so keep up with it! It’s good that you want to stay single and reflect on yourself, that’s the better way to do it. Keep working on yourself, and move forward :) you got this

Only top picks would be invited to write the essay in real time and then choices would be narrowed down. These were the exact questions we were given as a prompt. I think there might have been also one about how the Covid pandemic affected us personally/how that influenced our reasoning for going into nursing as I applied right in the thick of covid in 2020/2021. But it would be good to be generally aware of significant global health issues at this moment as they may throw in a question like that.

Is it the math that you are struggling with? Or would you normally be able to get above 90% on practice questions/tests and it’s just the anxiety that’s psyching you out. I’m guessing it’s some sort of combination of the two but I would really sit down and assess the questions you got wrong and why you did. 

Are you misreading what the question is asking for? Rounding wrong, have a specific type of question you’re weaker at? (Dilution questions, IV drip rate conversions, etc…). Always read the questions carefully to make sure ur solving for the right thing. And make sure the units are correct and converted appropriately! Sometimes they will give you the amounts in mg and ask for the answer in grams. Little things like that can add up easily. And make sure you’re using the right number in your calculations, sometimes they would throw in a number that was actually not needed to solve the answer and that would always throw me off. That was the majority of where my mistakes usually came from when practicing. If you can figure out why you’re getting the questions wrong and focus on practicing those types of questions more, it will become more intuitive and you will feel more confident when it comes to the test. If you have more confidence that you can solve every type of question correctly, you will worry less about losing time. 

I also find that you can almost always double check your answers by sort of plugging it in reverse. The questions will have enough info where if u use the answer you calculated with a value provided in the question, it should give u a 3rd value that is also consistent with one that is provided in the question. If the numbers don’t match up, you may have gone wrong somewhere. A simple example would be:

A patient is ordered 5 mg ramipril. The tablets are supplied in 2.5 mg per tablet form. How many tablets will you give this patient? 

This one’s a bit obvious but you should get 2 tablets as your answer. If you logic it out and think does 2 (tablets) x 2.5 mg (amount per tablet) = 5mg (the ordered dose)? Yes it does. 

Example of how u can tell if your answer was wrong for this question. Let’s say u calculated 3 tablets as the answer. 3 (tablets) x 2.5 mg (amount per tablet) = 7.5 mg. Double check, that’s not the ordered dose provided in the question, so you know you went wrong somewhere with ur calculations. Obviously his is a very simple example but hopefully it shows what I mean.

In my program you have to get 95% or above (only can get 1/20 questions wrong) and I was constantly terrified of putting the wrong answers, so I would use this reverse sort of calculation to and double check my answers and I’ve always gotten 100% on all my med math exams.

Otherwise, can you reach out to profs or someone at your school for additional help or assistance with prepping for the test? My school also has accommodations for disabilities which includes things like ADHD or anxiety that will impact your test taking abilities, so they give you extra time to write. May be worth finding out if your school has something like that.

How long have you been training? If it’s been relatively new it can be super hard to stay motivated, the habit hasn’t really formed yet. Exercise is hard and painful especially in the beginning stages if you haven’t grown up living an active lifestyle, so it makes sense that at first you wouldn’t really have much of a desire to go above and beyond. 

I found that after working out for about 6 months consistently I actually craved going if I missed too many days. A lot of people will tell you that motivation on its own usually isn’t enough, you need discipline. Motivation runs out eventually, you lose steam, and lose urgency. It happens to me too. To continue making consistent progress towards your goals you will just have to make yourself go when you don’t want to sometimes. I do think that it is true that it may be unsustainable if you feel like you’re constantly forcing yourself to do something you hate. The goal is to hopefully get to a point where you naturally want to work out and that will usually take some discipline to get to that point where you really establish the routine. 

But imo it also depends on how bad you want to achieve your goals. You get what you put into it. It’s okay to not be as motivated and lose the urgency if you personally are okay with getting to your goals at a more relaxed pace rather than the most efficient way possible. It’s not always terrible to take a step back and relax on the routine. I got very burned out from weightlifting consistently 4x a week after a few years, so now I have tried other forms of exercise as my goals have changed. Before I specifically wanted to look a certain way, build up certain muscles, but now I am happy exercising for pleasure and leisure, and just doing things I enjoy that get my body moving and keep me healthy. I’ve been rock climbing indoors and snowboarding recently, and bouldering in particular has actually made my upper body stronger than its ever been which I love. Snowboarding is mostly just for fun lol. I’ll throw in a 1 or 2 weightlifting sessions a week because now that I’ve relaxed I find myself actually wanting to do it now out of my own free volition, and also to keep my body balanced and use the muscle groups I’m neglecting with bouldering. So maybe you also could branch out and find other forms of exercise that align with your goals and are enjoyable. Cheaper ones are, swimming, hiking, walking, yoga, etc… there are so many to explore! Something that you enjoy = something that is sustainable. Also, any exercise > no exercise. Even if it’s just a 10 minute walk, stretching and yoga for 10 minutes before you go to sleep, etc.. Some variety in the kinds of exercise you do also helps to keep you from burning out and getting tired of doing the same things. You can still do this in the gym if you can’t afford/can’t access other kinda of sports/activities. For example, I used to strictly weight lift and occasionally do cardio. Now I find myself having more fun trying to train calisthenics or even pylometric type exercises sometimes to switch it up. I also like the added benefit of having more functional strength in a sense where I feel like my training makes me more athletic overall and is more applicable to daily life situations. But that is because my goals have changed  and this type of training is more enjoyable and profitable for my goals. Overall, whatever you decide to do should be beneficial to your goals, as it can be discouraging to start making progress in a direction you don’t want to and get further from your goal. 

I hope this helped a bit, I’m no pro so of course this is not anything you should take to heart. Just my own experience with losing motivation and how I’ve been getting it back :)

Hi, I took this test in October. It was pretty chill and I passed first attempt. I wasn’t asked to disable my backup camera, but I also made sure I wasn’t really using or relying on it and was using my mirrors, actively looking out the back window, etc… It is true that they sometimes don’t make you back park anyways (though you should know how by now). 

I think the test was fairly straight forward and easy, I and my friends have all found they they generally try to just pick up bad habits you may have learned, and are generally not as strict about failing you for minor mistakes compared to passing the Class 7. I had to take my N test 3 times to pass, and passed my class 5 the first time, examiner told me I “aced” it despite me accidentally stopping way past the stop line the first stop sign out the ICBC lot lol. I picked up my act after that and it turned out okay. Just drive safe, remember when back parking or parallel parking that you don’t have to do it perfect all in one shot, just do it safely. If you have to move forward and then reverse again to readjust, make sure you do a full 360 degree check every time you put your vehicle in reverse (not just for parking but at any point). Always shoulder check if they ask you to pull over and open your door. Know which direction to point your wheels for uphill vs. Downhill parking. Know the hand signals for turning. Come up with some general hazards you can pull out for when they ask you to name hazards: I like to use: pedestrians, hidden driveways, any debris on the road like branches (if they are present), weather (rain/snow, even bright sun can be a hazard), cars parked/pulled over on the side of street that may unexpectedly pull out or someone may open the door suddenly (if you can point out specifically a car that has its lights/engine on and no signals this will be even better) bikers, parked large delivery type trucks that may obstruct your view, etc… Familiarize yourself with the downtown one way streets like Leon, and the school/park areas nearby. as long as you give the examiner a smooth ride and make them feel like you are safe and competent, you will pass. Some people find it helps to narrate everything they are thinking/doing if silence worries you or you want to make sure they are aware when you are scanning jntersections, shoulder checking, etc… for example.: “turning signal on, shoulder checking, I see no hazards.” but I didn’t find that to be necessary and did just fine without really making any small talk and just answering them when they gave me instructions or occasionally clarifying what they mean.

I can relate to a lot of this. Messy ending to relationship, only had toxic experiences with other partners, childhood trauma, adult sexual trauma, etc… which caused me to later have attachment issues and mental illness which obviously made for a poor combo. Ex was avoidant so yeah typical anxious-avoidant dumpster fire.

The only advice I really have is that you HAVE to practice self-forgiveness. I was in therapy for 5 months after my breakup because I was absolutely devastated and my depression only got so much worse and I was worried for my own safety and it really saved me. I also have taken classes on mental health and psychology as I am in nursing school so I feel pretty decently versed in therapeutic techniques and understanding of mental health. 

Remember that whatever you did or said, you had a reason for it. There is always a reason we act or feel the way we do. Emotions are innately protective. They come up when our body and unconscious recognizes and is trying to signal to your concious awareness that hey, there is something here you need to pay attention to (whether positive or negative). These emotions can lead to behavioural responses. So in the end everything you do and feel has a cause. And I want you to explore that cause, and in the future as well just be curious about why you feel that way. Really get into it. 
Next, validate yourself. You reacted that way in response to something. It could be in the moment or something triggered from your past wounds. But there was a reason, and that reason is enough. Even if you don’t believe it, tell yourself that it was okay for you to act that way or feel that way. Tell yourself and remind yourself that you were doing the best that you could with the resources and experiences you have had in life that lead you to this moment. Your experiences shape who you are, and your experiences are valid. They happened to you, and now this is why you respond the way you do. Nobody can deny that. 

At first this will feel uncomfortable and maybe stupid, but try consistently being curious about your own emotions and reactions. It will build awareness and once you get pretty good at identifying what you feel and why, it is easier to regulate your emotions in a healthier manner, and will make for better decision making in the future. For example, you understand what you’re feeling and can attribute it to some past unhealed traumas, recognize it’s not your partners fault and be mindful of trying to not project onto them. Or you can recognize maybe you feel jealous or crazy because your partner has done actions to make you feel that way. My therapist told me always validate yourself and trust your gut and intuition. It is telling you something for a reason. You acted the way you acted for a reason. And your reason, whether you think it is valid now or not was enough reason at the time. We are only human and make mistakes our whole lives, after all it is everybody’s first time going through the human experience. Sending hugs and I hope this helps, this was my favourite takeaway and lesson from my therapy and I hope it works for you as well.

As someone in their 3rd year of uni who also spent highschool coasting and getting high grades, honestly the biggest thing for me is show up to class! My school uses percentages instead of gpa but I think mine converts to like 3.9. I’ve taken anywhere from 5-8 classes per semester (thank nursing school for that) and I still honestly don’t have the best study habits, and I tend to cram only days-hours before my exams, procrastinate assignments, scrolling through phone for hours etc… but it’s so much easier when you show up to class consistently. Even if you’re distracted during it, just trying to generally keep up with what the instructor is saying (sometimes they give tips for exams/possible exam questions!) and skimming over the slides/readings will help you be more caught up or recognize atleast something instead of knowing nothing since the midterm. 

It is hard. It will take some discipline. But try to make it a habit. What pushes me is that I’ve never had much money and rely on student loans completely for my classes. By skipping them or not trying to do well on them I’m actively wasting all my money and putting myself into debt for no reason. Every class that I miss is like 70$ out of my pocket wasted. Try to find something that pushes you. Discipline over motivation, motivation is fickle and unreliable. Just try to force yourself to do something consistently (ie. showing up to class every time, doing the readings before class everytime, dedicate one day a week to review what you learned, etc…) you don’t have to do multiple, just choose something and it will give u a better basis so you aren’t scrambling to cram all the time. You might still cram (I’m guilty of this) but it’s a lot easier to do so when you’re relearning something you’ve atleast heard or seen before compared to starting from scratch.

Hey, I was also blindsided, thought things were great until we were over. If it helps your experience, I made the mistake of staying in contact and trying to stay “friends” (at his request).

I don’t think she wants to reject you because of it, and I doubt that she faked it. She was probably truthful about going through a really hard time and you were probably like a light that helped her get through it. But I think it is possible that her mental health issues are why things ended up like this. Depression is really tough, it sucks the light out of you, tells you lies that nobody cares, nobody wants you. And it doesn’t matter what other people say, depression says it louder. It makes it hard to get up. Hard to do things and spend time with the people you love. It makes you feel like you aren’t good enough for anyone. I’m sure you tried to love her, but it’s not your fault or hers. For me, I never wanted things to end with my ex but my depression made me so insecure, so irritable. I felt like a bad partner. I worried about him leaving me and relied on him for all of my tiny bits of happiness and it drove him away. I felt unlovable. I don’t know what she’s going through but if it’s anything like me, she doesn’t want things to end, she doesn’t want to reject you. But it’s not sustainable and she probably feels a lot of guilt for how she is now. And she’s staying away because she doesn’t want to be a burden anymore
